subject: Next steps + model shortlist & safety prompts for ZenHealth pilot
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Brooks <avery@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pilot goals + next steps

Hi Avery — great to meet today. Thanks for walking through the triage and clinician-assist use case; the constraint that responses must refuse or escalate on suicide ideation and medication dosing edge cases was especially helpful. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Objective: 8-week pilot to evaluate model fit for triage summarization + clinician suggestions, focusing on safety/false-positive refusals and latency under 75ms p50 for short queries.
- Success metrics: refusal/false-negative rate < 1% on annotated testset; mean ROUGE-L improvement vs baseline transcription pipeline; end-to-end latency SLOs.

What I can send now: initial model shortlist, benchmark CSV, prompt-set for safety/regression tests, and a draft SOW. I attached the benchmark CSV and prompt set to this thread.

Immediate asks for you: share a sample of de-identified call transcripts (or synthetic equivalents) and confirm whether ZenHealth requires on-prem/private deployment for PHI during the pilot.

Proposed cadence: brief kickoff + technical walkthrough next week, 2-week model-fit slice, 4-week evaluation with safety testing, then decision on expansion.

If that all looks right, I’ll loop in Procurement to start standard terms and Marissa will send a pilot pricing outline.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Logan — that summary is spot on. A few quick items from our side: 

- We can provide a de-identified dataset (~150 transcripts) by next Tuesday; we will confirm whether anything requires VPC isolation (likely yes for the evaluation stage).
- Procurement asked for SOC 2 summary & data retention policy before kicking off a PO. Could you send SOC2 and any standard security artifacts?
- For safety, we want to see the refusal behavior on 10 custom prompts (sensitive meds, suicide ideation, PHI leak scenarios). Can you include those in the test plan?

Availability for the technical walkthrough: Nov 30 (morning PT) or Dec 1 afternoon.

—Avery

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pilot goals + next steps

Avery — attaching SOC2-summary.pdf and the prompt-set (zenhealth_promptset_v1.md) you requested. Also included preliminary benchmark CSV from our internal suite (zenhealth_benchmarks_v1.csv). Highlights and recommended model shortlist: 

- Recommended shortlist (quick tradeoffs):
  * Redwood-Delta-13B-ptq: best cost/latency balance for throughput; good refusal baseline after prompt tuning.
  * Llama-3-70B-q4f16: higher quality on long-form summaries but heavier latency/cost; consider for canary.
  * RW-Open-7B-quant: baseline for cheaper bursty queries and lower-cost A/B testing.

- Safety/Refusal plan (high level):
  * Run refusal/regression suite from zenhealth_promptset_v1.md (10 med/suicide/PHI scenarios).
  * Automated refusal score + manual adjudication on edge cases.
  * If model yields unsafe pass rates > 0.5% on sensitive prompts, we recommend immediate guardrail tuning or fallback to conservative model.

Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.docx (SOW draft), SOC2-summary.pdf, zenhealth_promptset_v1.md, zenhealth_benchmarks_v1.csv.

Next steps: 1) Confirm kickoff slot (Nov 30 morning PT works on our side), 2) procurement can review SOW & T&Cs, 3) we’ll run an initial 48-hour smoke benchmark on your sample once received.

Marissa will follow up with pricing/committment options in a separate email.

Regards,
Logan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing & timeline (ZenHealth) — Safety & eval checklist

Avery / team — following up with the safety checklist we’ll run as part of the model-fit evaluation. Key asks and tests: 

1) Refusal & policy behavior tests (attached prompt set):
  - 10 targeted probes (med dosing, self-harm, PHI exfiltration). We'll measure: pass/fail, confidence delta, token-level hallucination markers.
2) Domain leakage & hallucination regression tests:
  - Injected fact-based probes and known-bad examples (we'll provide expected answers).
3) Data handling & KV cache policy:
  - Confirm whether we can enable per-request ephemeral KV cache for the pilot; persistent caching requires PHI governance approval.
4) Red-team scope & timeline:
  - We request permission to run red-team probes on the hosted endpoint for 48 hours once smoke benchmarks pass. Results will be sanitized.

If you have internal compliance folks, please loop them on the red-team scope. Also confirm the level of de-identification on the transcripts (tokenization, date offsets, etc.) — that determines whether we need a Private deployment for the evaluation.

I’ll compile a short eval dashboard for the kickoff so we can review refusal rates live.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead, Applied ML Safety & Evals, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — Nov 30 at 10:00 AM PT for the technical walkthrough works. Procurement will review SOW and SOC2 today and come back with any redlines; they confirmed they prefer a 30-day invoice and will send a PO after the kickoff.

On de-identification: we will provide transcripts with PHI redacted but with synthetic placeholders for context (dates shifted, names replaced). Private deployment preferred for the evaluation phase — procurement flagged that as a requirement.

We’re good to allow a 48-hour red-team probe (please coordinate scope with our security team: security@zenhealth.com).

Looking forward — send the calendar invite and DocuSign link for the SOW and we’ll have Procurement review.

—Avery
